title: A Phone Call with an Old Friend
subtheme: A Phone Call with an Old Friend
description: Hear a familiar voice and share news in a phone conversation.
cardDescription: Hear a familiar voice and share news in a phone conversation.
focus: The setting is a Phone Call with an Old Friend. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Everyday short name for a telephone
Say a name to get attention

answerNotes.PHONE: Phone is the everyday short form of telephone. Older sets had dials and receivers; newer ones can also show video.
answerNotes.CALL: Call can mean telephone contact or saying a name aloud. Both uses involve trying to get someone's attention.
answerNotes.VOICE: A voice is the sound produced when someone speaks or sings. A speaker is the device that reproduces the sound on a call or recording.
answerNotes.HELLO: Hello is a greeting. It commonly opens a phone call, while goodbye marks the ending.
answerNotes.LISTEN: Listen means pay attention to a sound. Hearing a sound can happen without deliberately listening to it.
answerNotes.NUMBER: A number can count an amount or identify something. A telephone number identifies a connection rather than measuring its size.
answerNotes.DIAL: A dial can show numbers on a clock, telephone, or radio. Its marks identify times, phone choices, or station frequencies according to the object.
answerNotes.EAR: Ears receive sound. In an animal clue, the word usually asks for a body part rather than a call or other sound.
answerNotes.LINE: Line can mean a row, a drawn mark, or a fishing cord. The clue's action helps distinguish those meanings.

words: Picture card mailed with a short greeting
Image made with a camera or pencil
Location written on a mailed envelope
Letters delivered by the postal service

answerNotes.STAMP: Stamp can mean a postage label or a tool that leaves an ink impression. A mailed letter and a craft project use different senses.
answerNotes.ADDRESS: An address tells where mail should go. The recipient's name identifies the person, while the street, city, and postal code locate the destination.
answerNotes.HOME: Home can mean a dwelling or the local side in a sporting match. Read the clue before applying the familiar household meaning.
answerNotes.PEN: A pen writes with ink. A pencil uses graphite, which can usually be removed with an eraser.

words: Moving pictures shown on a screen

Device that makes a recorded voice audible
Small on-screen control pressed during a call
Word often said when answering a phone

answerNotes.SCREEN: Screen can mean a display surface or a mesh barrier. The phone and movie scenes use the display meaning; a porch door uses the mesh meaning.
answerNotes.CAMERA: A camera records pictures. Its lens focuses the scene, while a shutter or electronic control determines when light is recorded.
answerNotes.VOICE: A voice is the sound produced when someone speaks or sings. A speaker is the device that reproduces the sound on a call or recording.
answerNotes.CALL: Call can mean telephone contact or saying a name aloud. Both uses involve trying to get someone's attention.
answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
answerNotes.SPEAKER: A speaker can be a person talking or an audio device. In a video call's controls, it is the device that makes sound audible.
answerNotes.BUTTON: A button fastens through a buttonhole or loop. Some have holes through the face; others attach by a small shank on the back.
answerNotes.MUTE: Muting stops a microphone from sending sound. It does not necessarily turn off the camera or end a video call.
answerNotes.HELLO: Hello is a greeting. It commonly opens a phone call, while goodbye marks the ending.

Calendar period divided into twelve months

answerNotes.CARD: Card can mean a printed greeting or a playing piece. An envelope points to a greeting; a deck or suit points to a game.
answerNotes.CANDLE: A candle burns fuel from its wax through a wick. Its flame produces light as the warmed wax is consumed.
answerNotes.ENVELOPE: An envelope encloses a letter. The destination goes on its front; the message stays inside.
answerNotes.STAMP: Stamp can mean a postage label or a tool that leaves an ink impression. A mailed letter and a craft project use different senses.
answerNotes.GIFT: A gift is something given, rather than sold. A tag identifies the recipient; wrapping protects or decorates the present.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.

answerNotes.NOTE: A note is a short written message. It can be a reminder, a greeting, or a brief explanation attached to an object.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.LIST: A list records items in order. Checking off a purchased item is different from changing the price or quantity of it.
answerNotes.PEN: A pen writes with ink. A pencil uses graphite, which can usually be removed with an eraser.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.PHONE: Phone is the everyday short form of telephone. Older sets had dials and receivers; newer ones can also show video.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.
